measurement:bootcamp-positions.note: Curated boot-camp positions. S1/S2: X,Z measured from the verified footage radar, Y decoded from the adv_bootcamp map heightmap (t000007c1_terrain.glm, context 1985). S4 adds enemy standing positions from the client nameplate range readout (client/ui/overheadwindow.pyo _UpdateEntityRange shows ceil(distance)) plus radar player position and heading, the client map cursor readout for indicator 437, and Y from the heightmap or the derived adv_bootcamp navmesh (bias-calibrated against six references). Each position record states its method, uncertainty and frames. S5/S6 add radar objective-indicator icons told apart from creature pips by the client radar code (client/ui/radarwindow.pyo HandleUpdateObjectiveIndicators, _GetEntityRadarType), third-person camera-ray triangulation for the bomb, the nameplate range readout for the outpost Thrax, inferred reinforcement bearings on the pad, the original damaged-pad map anchor for the exit, and the Alia Das arrival from the wilderness radar texture with Y from the derived adv_foreas_concordia_wilderness navmesh. The Rogers turn-in (GAP-ROGERS) adds his command-tent position in context 1220 from the yellow handset radar icon (template NCC with per-frame wilderness radar matching) with Y from the derived wilderness navmesh. The Wilderness arrival (W1) adds Training Officer Kincaid in context 1220 from the yellow handset radar icon beside the barracks tent (one viewpoint, check SEG3-03), corroborated by the client map marker "Class Trainer: Alia Das".

gaps.summary: Collection objectives have no counter. The client skeleton carries conversation bindings but no npc_mission_objective_counter rows at all - the only counter row in the world is the one the S4 slice seeded for 1994 - so a mission whose objective is "Acquire 8 Boargar Cell Samples" (751) or "Collect twelve Thrax hearts" (479) can only be seeded as conversation-only, which would let the collection be skipped. The bulk generator therefore selects only missions whose every objective is conversation-bound and held 751 back; the counter-driven ones (479, 489, 665, 751, 758, 780 and the rest) wait for the loot-counter mechanism. That mechanism needs two things: a way for looted items to advance a counter, and the drop source for each item, since item loot tables are not in the world seed either.

gaps.summary: Mission 1992 'Gearing Up for Battle' stalled at objective 1 ('Get your gear from the nearby crate') in live play on 2026-09-16 (character 5: objective 4 complete, objective 1 open). First written up as three missing ContentRuleEvent kinds; that diagnosis was wrong. The objective bindings for 1992/1 (loot_all on crate 198651), 1992/2 (equip any), 1992/3 and 1992/8 (hit on dummies 198652/198653) were seeded by BootcampS2GearingUp, load with 0 gaps, and their runtime paths exist and are tested. The actual defect: the crate's loot window rows were built from bare item template ids with fresh entity ids and no item behind them, while the client's corpselootwindow resolves every row with GetEntity(itemId) and skips one it cannot resolve - so the window listed nothing to take - and the window's right-click path (RequestLootItemFromCorpse, one row at a time) was never routed to content containers. Character 5's inventory confirms it: only the creation kit (templates 145, 13126, 13186, 13156, 28, all created 2026-09-15 17:01:10) and nothing from item set 19858; the 'gear' the player equipped was the starter armour.
gaps.closes_with: content containers hold real items, created once per owner from the item set and introduced to the client (SendItemDataToClient) before LootInfo/CanLootItems, as RequestCorpseLooting already does for corpses; RequestLootItemFromCorpse on a content container routes to RequestLootItemFromContentContainer; Loot All takes every row that fits, like the corpse dispenser; the loot_all binding completes when the container is empty by either path. Tests: MissionLogTests ContentContainerRowsAreRealItemsIntroducedBeforeTheWindowOpens, TakingContainerItemsOneAtATimeCompletesTheObjectiveOnTheLastOne, TakingAnUnknownOrAlreadyTakenContainerRowChangesNothing, LootAllTakesWhatIsLeftAfterSingleTakes. Not established: whether the original completed the objective when the crate was emptied one row at a time; the footage shows only Loot All (A3-017 to A3-024).

gaps.summary:
CLOSED and confirmed in live play on 2026-09-18 22:23 UTC. Fourth diagnosis, and the first that reached the entity class. The crate is entity class 26714 UsableTreasureDispHumCrateV04, chosen under OD-12 as 'the first TreasureDispenser candidate' - picked by name, never checked against the loot protocol. Its only augmentation is 64 TreasureDispenser, 'Usable: drops loot into inventory (or world) when used', and the client's treasuredispenser augmentation carries no Recv_ handlers at all: __init__, IsClosed, IsCipherable. Every window method the server was sending - LootInfo, CanLootItems, TakenInfo and the LootCorpse added earlier the same day - belongs to augmentation 50 LootDispenser, so the client dropped all of them. Exactly two classes in the entire client carry 50, Sys_LootDispenser (3331) and CorpseLootDispenser (10000035), and neither is a crate, so no class swap can give the crate a window.

The original had one. Footage A3-017 (t=304.733) shows a window headed 'Supply Crate' listing the items with a 'Loot All' button, A3-022 the five rows, A3-023 the 'You received 1 ...' lines and A3-024 the objective completing. A loot dispenser is attached to the crate - which is what LootDispenser.AttachedTo is for and what every corpse does - and the window takes its heading from the attached entity. From there the corpse machinery serves it: the client addresses the dispenser's entity id, FindLootable finds it in MapChannel.LootDispensers, and taking, Loot All and the settle are the paths already proven in play. The content layer now only opens the window and completes the objective when the container is empty, and the three loot handlers no longer need a content-container special case at all.

Three earlier diagnoses were wrong or incomplete: missing rule kinds (wrong); rows built from bare template ids with no item behind them (real, and fixed, but not why the window was empty); and the missing LootCorpse (real, and necessary, but sent to an entity that cannot receive it).

gaps.summary: The navmesh reads high on terrain, so 'on the navmesh surface' was never the same as 'on the floor'. Measured 2026-09-17 against everything in the world at once: the original server's own 217 creature spawns sit a median 0.276 m below the surface, its 357 teleporters 0.150 m below it, and the three characters' own client-reported standing positions 0.08, 0.31, 0.41 and 0.47 m below it - a body demonstrably on the floor reads under the navmesh, because Recast's walkable surface is the top of a voxel column rather than the terrain under it. The floor is therefore taken to be surface - 0.276 m, the offset the original spawns sit at, and WorldPositionAudit measures bodies against that with a 0.5 m tolerance instead of 2.0 m against the raw surface. The bias is a terrain effect and not a constant: the grating platform's top, taken from the client's own map file at 122.11, matches the navmesh there to 0.01 m, so nothing was re-snapped wholesale - WorldPlacementFloorSnap moved only the 14 rows more than 0.5 m off.
evidence: rasaworld.db spawnpool and teleporter tables (original server data)
gaps.closes_with: a navmesh rebuild whose surface lands on the terrain, or a per-map measurement of the bias
surfaced_by: live play 2026-09-17 ("thrax infantry is in the ground too")

gaps.summary:
Two NPCs created by earlier W3 batches carry a dialogue package that belongs to someone else, so they speak the wrong lines and their own objectives stay dead ends. Found 2026-09-17 by reading each package's full usage across the client's objectiveconversation table instead of one mission at a time.

Field Lt. Brody (creature 199105) carries package 550, whose line is the rescued squad member's "Man, am I glad you showed up ... get back to Brody" - spoken TO the player ABOUT Brody, so it cannot be his. Brody's own package is 145, which completes 361/1 ("Report to Field Lieutenant Brody who is stationed at the Walk of Giants") and 670/2 ("return to Field Lieutenant Brody"). Package 550 belongs to Captain Fransisco, the survivor in Devil's Den, who is client name 6587 and is not in the world at all.

Captain Reyko (creature 199502) carries package 1213, whose line is a machine's: "This console appears to have an active communications system. You should be able to contact Captain Reyko from here." Reyko's own package is 1200, which completes four missions that all name him - 1113/7, 1125/1, 1310/1 and the 20000003 Halloween mission.

Neither can be corrected on its own: moving Brody to 145 leaves 550 unbound until Fransisco exists, and moving Reyko to 1200 leaves 1213 unbound until the console is dispensed as a usable. The npc_package table keys on the creature id, so one creature cannot carry two. Update 2026-09-19 (DevilsDenFransisco): the Brody half is closed - Captain Fransisco stands in the Devil's Den at TaRapedia's coordinates with package 550 and Brody carries his own 145, so 670 can be finished and 361/1 is bound. Reyko remains: moving him to 1200 would bind 1113/7, 1125/1 and 1310/1 but unbind 1112/1 until the console is placed, and no source gives the console's position. Closed 2026-09-19: Brody carries 145 with Captain Fransisco seeded for 550, and Reyko carries his own 1200. The console half is now GAP-W3-UNBOUND-CONVERSATION-PACKAGE's 1112/1.

gaps.summary:
Closed 2026-09-18. 'Shoot the Practice Dummy' (1992/3) could not advance because the dummy could not be targeted. The client-method trace showed StartAutoFire/AutoFireKeepAlive/StopAutoFire and never SetTargetId, and the server's new miss log showed every shot as 'fired action WeaponAttack at entity 0'. The client's targeting.py SetDirectTarget - the only place it sends SetTargetId - returns False when the entity's GetTargetCategory() is None, and for the dummy's augmentation (41 InertDestroyable) that category is set only by Recv_TargetCategory from the server. DynamicObjectManager never sent one. Creatures always had one, by coincidence correct: TargetCategoryPacket was typed Factions, and Bane=0 / AFS=1 happen to equal the client's HOSTILE/FRIENDLY; the type could never say OBJECT=2. The packet now takes the client's own targetdata values (TargetCategory), creatures send Hostile/Friendly by faction explicitly, and dynamic objects send Object.

The category alone was not enough - the next live attempt (2026-09-19 01:59) still sent no SetTargetId. Firing a weapon sets targeting's target type to Hostile (_GetTargetTypeForAction), and under Hostile _IsTargetType only admits a non-hostile entity when IsDirectTargetable(), which in usable.py requires canBeDamaged. That flag starts from the client's own usabledata row for the class, and for 29365 the row is (None, None, None, None, None): the server is expected to say, through Recv_DamageInfo. DamageInfoPacket existed in the server and was never sent. Dynamic objects with hit points are now introduced with DamageInfo(canBeDamaged, not repairable, max, current).

gaps.summary: Closed 2026-09-19 (OD-56). The server never rolls a critical hit: HitData.IsCritical is always 0. gaps.summary: Closed 2026-09-19. Nothing regenerates on this branch: health, power and armour refresh amounts are computed but no refresh period is ever set and the server never ticks them, so the client predicts no regeneration either. The worn armour's regen rate (its tooltip's 'Regen Rate: 1 per sec') is summed and unused. Regeneration Wave's bonus, Base Wave's armour regeneration and Disease's 'stops regeneration' therefore have nothing to act on. ellimist/development has 'Tell players when they are in combat, and make regeneration exist' (94b4485). Now: health, power and armour regenerate each second (HEALTH/POWER/ARMOR_REGEN_PERIOD = 1), a fifth in combat (IN_COMBAT_REGEN_MODIFIER = 0.2, on the amount because Actor.UpdateAttribute resets the period to 1), armour at the worn pieces' RegenRate times any EFFECT_ARMOR_REGEN_MODIFIER (Base Wave 500). Inferred: health and power at 2 x Regeneration Rate / 100 a second, and combat lasting 15 s after the last damage. Creatures still do not regenerate.
evidence: ManifestationManager.UpdateStatsValues: no RefreshPeriod assignment; armorRegenRate unused

owner_decisions.decision: Trigger radii for objective and area triggers
owner_decisions.default: Use the inferred radius
owner_decisions.choice: An objective or area trigger takes a larger radius than a bare reading of the measurement suggests - enough that a player crossing the intended place cannot miss it - but not so large that it fires from outside that place. The radius is a reconstruction parameter, not a recovered value, and every use says so. Applied so far: S1's two bridge objectives 4 m -> 10 m (the ceremonial bridge is 16.8 m wide and a recruit crossed it without touching the 4 m sphere), and 1994's cave-in trigger 5 m -> 10 m.

owner_decisions.decision: Objectives that collect a creature drop
owner_decisions.default: Count the deaths of the creature the objective names
owner_decisions.choice: An objective like "Get 6 Miasma Goo Samples" needs three things: the item, the creature that drops it and the drop itself. The client gives the first two - the item is its own physical entity class (Miasma Goo 11162, Xanx Pincers 11160) and the objective's own words name the creature family, which the world seed carries (Bane Miasma 88, Bane Shield Drone 85, Bane Xanx 87) - but no surviving source ties a mission item to an item template or to a loot table, so the drop cannot be reconstructed. Until it can, such an objective is bound as a count of that creature's deaths, which is what it means in play. Every field keeps its own tier: the creature and the item class are original, the target comes from the objective's text, and the binding is the reconstruction this decision authorises. A later pass with drop data would replace the binding with a real loot counter.

owner_decisions.default: Cluster the specimens around the mission's own area
owner_decisions.choice: No surviving source records a creature spawn: the world seed carries 155 creatures, all Wilderness, the original dump's creature_type has 21 rows and no client table has spawn data. Where a mission names a species the client carries as an entity class (Lasher 7477, Magmonix 6338, Stalker 3781), the species is reconstructed: its class, name and the mission's own numbers are original, but its **positions** are analogues - a cluster of specimens around the area the mission's own sources put it in, one specimen more than the objective asks for, with a respawn so the cluster recovers. Health and respawn delay are analogues too, taken from the world's comparable Bane creatures. Every such field is recorded as an analogue with this decision, and the user authorised this reconstruction on 2026-09-16. The respawn delay is 60000 ms and is documented here rather than on each placement row, because content_placement.respawn_ms is an optional column and the manifest's rule is to leave an optional column out rather than fill it with an analogue.

owner_decisions.decision: Creature loot: the original table, and the stand-in for everything else
owner_decisions.default: Roll the surviving rows; keep the emulator's stand-in drop for creatures with no rows
owner_decisions.choice: The original server kept loot per creature type (creature_type_loot: itemTemplateId, chance as a float, stacksizeMin, stacksizeMax), and this world's creature table is that same type table. Exactly seven rows survived, all belonging to one type - the raiding trainee Thrax footsoldier - so the mechanism is implemented in the original's shape and those seven rows are seeded on this world's Thrax soldiers. Every other creature keeps the emulator's stand-in drop (one stack of item 28 on a coin flip) rather than paying out nothing, because paying out nothing would be a behaviour change based on missing data rather than on evidence; GAP-CREATURE-LOOT names what would replace it.

owner_decisions.default: A placement whose creature walks with the player on its mission; an area objective on that mission needs the escort inside it
owner_decisions.choice: The original's escort objectives ("Take Milpas to Apirka", "Escort Milpas to Divide entrance") are area objectives with a condition the emulator did not have: the creature being escorted has to arrive too. content_placement gained an escort_mission_id and a third behavior (Escort); the creature follows the player on that mission, re-pathing at most every two seconds, and the area objective only completes once the escort is inside the area. Milpas' class and level follow the OD-45 pipeline and his name id is the client's own ('Ranger Milpas', 9519); the destinations are Warrior Apirka's recorded position and the world's own Wilderness->Divide map link.

owner_decisions.default: Both are implemented from the client's own opcodes and the mission flags the seed carries
owner_decisions.choice:
Two mission features were withheld by design: Mission.DefinitionGaps() added "radio completion is not implemented" and "mission sharing is not implemented" for every definition flagged radio_completeable or shareable, which kept those missions out of the game entirely. Both are implemented now, from the only evidence that exists - the client's own requests (missionlog.pyo: CompleteRadioMission and RewardRadioMission carry (missionId, selectionIdx, rating); ShareMission carries (missionId); AssignSharedMission and DeclineSharedMission carry (playerId, missionId)) and the flags in npc_mission, which decide what the client's mission log offers rather than what the server allows.

Radio: the NPC turn-in's payout was split out of its NPC-specific checks (receiver id and conversation range) into MissionManager.PayOut, and CompleteRadioMission reaches it while requiring the radio_completeable flag. RewardRadioMission carries the identical tuple, so it goes through the same path - which cannot double-pay, because a completed mission is no longer completeable. Which of the two the client sends for the completion and which for the reward claim is NOT established: GAP-W3-RADIO-REWARD-STEP.

Sharing: the mission goes into the party member's log at share time and the sharer is recorded as a pending share; accepting clears it and declining drops the mission back out. Whether the original logged the mission at share time or only on acceptance is NOT established - missionlog.pyo has the accept and decline requests, but no surviving data has the offer packet: GAP-W3-SHARING-OFFER.

owner_decisions.default: The client's own protocol and its own catalogue and duration tables
owner_decisions.choice:
The auction house's handlers were ToDo stubs - every request logged and ignored, and the creation path sent one of each failure message in a loop. It is implemented from two pieces of the client itself. The replies are the ones the client's own handlers expect, recovered from client/auctionhouse.pyo in the client protocol inventory (AuctionCreationSuccess(itemId), AuctionCreationFailed(itemId, message), QuerySuccess(itemList), QueryFailed(message), AuctionStatusSuccess(itemList), AuctionStatusFailed(message), AuctionBuyoutSuccess(itemId), AuctionBuyoutFailed(itemId, message), CancelAuctionSuccess(itemId), CancelAuctionFailed(itemId, message), AuctionSold(itemId, price), AuctionExpired(itemId)) - CreationSuccess, CreationFailed, QuerySuccess and QueryFailed already existed; the other eight are new. The parameters are the client's own tables: the four listing durations with the deposit each costs (5%, 10%, 20%, 25%) and the 83-row catalogue the browse window filters by, matched to an item through its class name (its parent/leaf pairs: Weapon contains Weapon_Pistol, Armor contains Armor_MotorAssist).

Three things the original had and no source shows are stated rather than invented: listings live in memory for the session, so a restart ends every auction; the seller is paid the full buyout price with no commission; and a sold or expired item goes straight into its owner's inventory instead of a pickup window. All three are GAP-W3-AUCTION-PERSISTENCE.

owner_decisions.default: The client's own recipes, consumed from the player's inventory
owner_decisions.choice: Every crafting request was declined with "not available on this server yet" - the manager's own doc said the recipes were the next step. The recipes are the client's: shared/crafting.pyo's recipeItemTemplateTable holds 160 schematics, each naming its inputs (an item template and a quantity), its result (template and amount), its energy cost, its KraftwerksTimeSeconds and the level it needs - and schematic 641 spells the whole chain out as 500 of item 1765 into 500 of item 28 (standard-grade cartridges) in five seconds at level 1. Fabrication now resolves the schematic (from the item the player is carrying in the 1.16.5 window's form, or from the recipe id in the older one), requires its level, plans every input against the player's own inventory before consuming anything, takes them with the same tested stack-consumption path item use takes, and starts a job whose time is the recipe's own. Collection (RequestRetrieveFinishedCraftItem and RetrieveAllFinishedItems) checks the station's clock before handing the item over, and creates the item only then, so an uncollected job holds no item row. Salvaging, module extraction, integration and upgrading still decline: their Mimeogel costs are in the same client table, but their item side is not in the emulator (GAP-W3-CRAFTING-MODULES).
